note: Discovery leads for cybersecurity topic workers (phase 2). LITERACY + awareness level with a defensive framing: teach what the concepts are, why they matter, and how to think about protection — NEVER how to attack. No step-by-step attack techniques, no exploit details, no malware source. Keep claims sourced and time-anchored where the landscape changes.

tierA.useFor: NIST Cybersecurity Framework (nist-cybersecurity-framework), NIST SP 800-series concepts (identity, authentication, least privilege, incident response)
threat advisories, phishing/social-engineering awareness, ransomware guidance, cyber hygiene
application-security risk concepts (threats, vulnerabilities, risk framing)

tierB.useFor: identity, MFA, zero trust, network security fundamentals (public pages read live)
awareness topics (phishing, password security) — public pages only
network, TLS/HTTPS, encryption explainers (public pages read live)

cautions: DEFENSIVE FRAMING ONLY: describe threats and attacks at the conceptual level (what they are, how they work in general, how to defend). NEVER provide step-by-step attack instructions, exploit code, or tool-specific attack workflows. If a source contains attack detail, paraphrase only the defensive-relevant parts.
LITERACY LEVEL: no tools, no command lines, no pentesting. Teach concepts and best practices; keep claims modest and sourced.
LEGAL/ETHICAL: state plainly that unauthorized access to systems is illegal; the lessons are about protection and awareness, not offensive skills.

NO INDIVIDUALIZED ADVICE: password/mfa lessons give general best practices (long passphrases, password managers, MFA enablement) without credential-handling or corporate policy specifics. Time-anchor threat trends (e.g. 'as of the cited source').

DEFINITIONAL DISTINCTIONS MUST BE CLEAN: threats vs vulnerabilities vs risk (the classic trio); authentication vs authorization; encryption vs hashing (encryption is reversible, hashing is one-way); viruses vs worms vs trojans vs ransomware (malware families); firewalls vs network segmentation (defense layers).

Distribute question answer keys EVENLY across A/B/C/D, ensuring at least one C and one D per topic. Verify keys yourself from the file, and avoid reusing identical question-stem templates across topics.
